scores.claim_text: Bell military aircraft and support programs revenue rose 28% to $2.618B in 2025, primarily on higher volume on the MV-75 program (the Army's V-280-based Future Long-Range Assault Aircraft).
scores.M_value: pentagon_jbook signal=NOT_FOUND for MV-75 / FLRAA / Future Long-Range Assault Aircraft / V-280 Valor (corpus coverage gap — the 410-PE corpus is heavy on Air Force / Space Force / DARPA / MDA / SOCOM RDT&E and does not appear to include Army Aircraft procurement / FLRAA RDT&E line). USAspending CONFIRMS Bell Textron Inc holds Army contract W58RGZ23C0001 ('FUTURE VERTICAL LIFT (FVL) FLRAA CAPABILITY SET THREE') with $3.537B obligated, plus $13.75B in cumulative DoD obligations across 25 surfaced awards — the FLRAA contract is real and is the largest single line in the surfaced sample.
scores.interpretation: Mark UNVERIFIABLE on the J-Book primary verifier per heuristic #7 (NOT_FOUND when company names a program clearly outside corpus scope is not a red flag). Independent USAspending cross-check (orthogonal verification) confirms the underlying $3.5B+ FLRAA award exists and is consistent with the company's narrative that MV-75 drove +$570M Bell military revenue in 2025. Coverage gap noted; this claim cannot be falsified with the present J-Book corpus.

scores.claim_text: Textron expects to be awarded the long-lead Low-Rate Initial Production (LRIP) phase of the MV-75/FLRAA contract in late 2026 or early 2027, with a $1.3 billion prototype testing & evaluation award already in backlog.
scores.M_value: pentagon_jbook NOT_FOUND for MV-75 LRIP / contractor 'Bell Textron'. earmark_detector returned NOT_EARMARK for FLRAA (program is a program of record, not a congressional add — the unfunded-by-earmark-sunset failure mode is not in play here). USAspending shows the $3.537B FLRAA capability-set-3 award is on contract and active.
scores.interpretation: J-Book corpus gap prevents direct forward-funding test of FLRAA LRIP. However: (a) the program is NOT an earmark, so the earmark-sunset failure mode is ruled out; (b) the $1.3B prototype T&E backlog addition is consistent with a program transitioning from EMD toward LRIP; (c) USAspending shows the contract is live and large. No J-Book disconfirmation available — UNVERIFIABLE.

scores.claim_text: The Future Attack Reconnaissance Aircraft (FARA) program — for which Bell had been a competitor — wound down, materially lowering 2024 Bell R&D and producing a $56M Bell R&D increase year-over-year in 2025.
scores.M_value: pentagon_jbook NOT_FOUND for FARA / Future Attack Reconnaissance Aircraft (corpus does not include Army Aviation RDT&E PEs).
scores.interpretation: The company itself discloses that FARA wound down — this is an admission against interest (lost competition / discontinued program), not a forward-looking claim. The narrative cost-flow (lower 2024 Bell R&D from FARA wind-down rebounding +$56M in 2025 from MV-75) is internally consistent. This claim does not depend on a J-Book look-up to be credible; treating as PASS on a disclosure-honesty basis. Coverage-gap caveat noted.

scores.claim_text: Textron Systems' Shadow UAS program was cancelled and certain U.S. Government development programs were terminated, lowering Systems volume and mix in 2025.
scores.M_value: pentagon_jbook NOT_FOUND for Shadow / RQ-7 Shadow / Shadow UAS (Army Aircraft Procurement / Other Procurement lines for RQ-7 not in corpus). USAspending query for 'Textron Systems' returned API server-disconnect (no obligations data surfaced this call); company's parent 'Textron Inc' shows 9,218 awards / $24.5B cumulative.
scores.interpretation: Company is openly disclosing a NEGATIVE program outcome (Shadow cancellation + DoD development-program terminations). This is the opposite of the J-Book-divergence failure mode the cohort targets (where management hides a program loss). Honest disclosure → PASS. The disclosure also explains why Textron Systems segment revenue was flat (+$6M) despite the SSC ramp.

scores.claim_text: Textron Systems' backlog grew 27% to $3.304B, including $480M for additional units on the Ship-to-Shore Connector (SSC) program and $475M for a five-year ATAC U.S. Navy Fighter Jet Services contract.
scores.M_value: pentagon_jbook NOT_FOUND for Ship-to-Shore Connector / SSC LCAC / ATAC Adversary Air / Contracted Air Services. Navy Ship & Aircraft Procurement lines and Navy CAS contracted-services lines are not in the present 410-PE corpus (which is focused on Air Force/Space Force/DARPA/MDA RDT&E + AF Procurement).
scores.interpretation: Both SSC and ATAC are established programs-of-record (SSC = LCAC replacement; ATAC = Navy adversary-air services). Backlog additions are consistent with normal program execution. No J-Book disconfirmation possible — UNVERIFIABLE per heuristic #7. Notably the backlog growth (+$710M, 27%) is the strongest forward indicator at Textron Systems and partially offsets the Shadow cancellation.

scores.claim_text: Approximately 27% of Textron's 2025 revenues (~$4.0B) were derived from contracts with the U.S. Government, including foreign military sales — making U.S. Government defense spending a load-bearing driver of consolidated results.
scores.M_value: USAspending: 'Textron Inc' returned 9,218 awards / $24.47B cumulative DoD obligations; 'Bell Textron Inc' returned 8,397 awards / $13.75B. The single largest line (Bell W58RGZ23C0001, $3.537B) is the FLRAA capability-set-3 award.
scores.interpretation: USAspending CONFIRMS material DoD revenue concentration consistent with 27% of $14.799B = ~$4.0B annual DoD revenue. Cross-check fully supports the disclosure. PASS.

scores.claim_text: On the upcoming MV-75 LRIP award, Textron expects an unfavorable cumulative catch-up program adjustment of $60-$110M reflecting higher-than-anticipated costs vs. original bid, though the overall MV-75 program will continue to generate positive margin.
scores.M_value: pentagon_jbook NOT_FOUND for FLRAA in the present corpus (coverage gap). Management is pre-disclosing a $60-110M unfavorable cum-catch-up on a fixed-price LRIP — this is a self-disclosed underdelivery on the bid economics.
scores.interpretation: This is a soft RED FLAG by management's own admission: they are warning that the FLRAA program — Bell's largest forward growth driver — was BID below the cost-to-produce, and the gap will materialize as a $60-110M loss adjustment upon LRIP option exercise on a fixed-price contract. The framework should flag this as MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY on the BID DISCIPLINE / PROFITABILITY axis even though absolute funding flow (per USAspending) is robust. The structural risk is that fixed-price defense programs in EMD-to-LRIP transition have a long history of cost overruns far exceeding initial estimates; the $60-110M range is a floor, not a ceiling.

scores.claim_text: Textron Aviation (commercial) delivered 171 Citation jets and 146 commercial turboprops in 2025, generating $5.955B of revenue (+13%) — a non-J-Book commercial cohort that should remain stable regardless of DoD program funding.
scores.M_value: Control claim; commercial business jet deliveries are reported quantitatively (171 Citation jets, +20 YoY; 146 turboprops, +19 YoY). Revenue and segment profit figures internally consistent.
scores.interpretation: Non-J-Book control passes — commercial Citation/turboprop figures are specific, quantitative, and internally consistent. No DoD-budget exposure on this revenue line.

scores.claim_text: Textron operates 57 U.S. plants and 45 plants outside the U.S. (102 total) with approximately 23.8 million square feet of manufacturing space, of which 59 are owned.
scores.M_value: Standard facility disclosure under Item 2; control claim for blinding test.
scores.interpretation: Routine Item 2 disclosure; no J-Book exposure; PASS.

scores.claim_text: Textron Specialized Vehicles divested its Powersports business in April 2025, reducing Industrial revenue by $195M and contributing to a $302M (9%) Industrial segment revenue decline.
scores.M_value: Disposition disclosed under Note 15; Industrial revenue walk attributes $195M of the $294M Specialized Vehicles decline to the disposition, with the remainder to golf-products volume.
scores.interpretation: Clean disposition disclosure; numeric walk is internally consistent. Non-defense, non-J-Book; PASS.
